author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: At 00:00 UTC on 24 February 2022 markets were pricing a March Fed lift-off and a still-pending escalation risk from the Donbas deployment at the same time: the S&P 500 in correction at 4,225.50 with the VIX at 31.02, the 2Y at 1.58% after a +56 bps 20-observation bear flattening (10Y-2Y +41 bps), Brent at 96.84 USD/bbl and TTF +25.34% over five sessions, while the last five observations show haven buying at the long end (10Y -6 bps). The stance is defensive: underweight long-duration growth, euro-area banks and Polish banks/discretionary, overweight energy, commodity producers (fertiliser, aluminium, gold miners) and defence primes, hold 10Y Treasuries as the hedge and prefer onshore China over offshore internet. The call changes on a credible diplomatic/summit track (cover European shorts first) or on an escalation beyond the separatist regions with broader sanctions (add to energy/gas, cut European financials).
sources_policy: Only the 2022-02-24 frozen feed (tools/digest.py, own-date exclusions applied) and the 2022-02-24 market card (tools/showcard.py) were used; no other date's feed, card, spec, draft or note and no web access. Every number comes from the card (exact values, card session tags) or from a headline cited in the same part; each citation ID is used at most twice; no numeric spot-FX (DXY only); previews are used only to establish pending events and no event dates are given without a dated headline; every 23 Feb-stamped item was screened for post-cutoff content, and the invasion appears only as a pending risk with two-sided scenarios.
